能管是日本傳統氣鳴樂器，屬橫吹竹笛，主要用於能劇與歌舞伎劇場音樂，也應用於寄席囃: The nōkan is a traditional Japanese aerophone, a side-blown bamboo flute used mainly in the theatre music of Nō and kabuki, and also in settings such as yosebayashi and Gionbayashi. The source names no particular composer or piece, so listening examples can only be understood through the occasions of use: in Nō and kabuki it takes part in the theatre music with a high, forceful tone, and in yosebayashi and Gionbayashi it appears as part of the ensemble of the performance concerned.
能管琴身以竹製成，傳統材料為川竹（又稱苦竹、篠竹），亦有用乾燥煤竹者。竹材劈開後: The body of the nōkan is bamboo, traditionally kawadake (also called nigadake or shinodake), and dried smoked bamboo is also used. The bamboo is split and cut into tapering strips, which are glued into a conical tube, with the hard face of the bamboo often turned inwards to improve the sound; in modern instruments the inner wall may be coated. The outside is bound with birch-cherry bark and lacquered, and the area around the fingerholes is reinforced with lacquer. The sounding parts include a lead cylinder inserted in the head joint above the blowing edge, wrapped in paper and wax, and a bamboo tube 2 to 3 mm thick inserted at the throat. The materials of the other parts are not stated.
能管起源於15世紀日本，由觀阿彌與其子世阿彌在改良能劇形式田樂、猿樂的過程中創造: The nōkan originated in fifteenth-century Japan, created by Kan'ami and his son Zeami as they refined the Nō forms of dengaku and sarugaku. It went on to serve not only Nō but also kabuki, yosebayashi and Gionbayashi and other traditional theatre music. The important change is in making: traditionally each instrument was fine-tuned by its maker, so the main frequency varied from one to the next; today some makers replace the inward-facing hard bamboo inner surface with a coating in order to keep the sound consistent.
能管音色尖銳明亮，具有穿透力強的高頻特質，帶有獨特的鼻音共鳴，音域集中在高音區。: The nōkan's timbre is sharp and bright, with the strongly penetrating high-frequency quality and the distinctive nasal resonance of an instrument whose range lies in the treble. The special sound produced by its “throat” gives the tone a subtle quiver and a bleak, weathered colouring. Compared with the crisp softness of a dizi, the nōkan sounds more fierce and grating; compared with the round transparency of the Western flute, it has more of an Eastern, mysterious, world-weary quality. Its resonance comes mainly from the bamboo body and the particular design of the throat, which give the sound wave a cavity of its own. This bright timbre with its Eastern colouring makes the nōkan an important instrument for building a deep theatrical atmosphere in Japanese classical music, and it suits above all the yūgen imagery of traditional Nō.
能管（Nōkan）是日本傳統高音橫吹竹笛，屬氣鳴樂器。它以劈開竹條黏合成漸細圓錐: The nōkan is a traditional Japanese high-pitched side-blown bamboo flute, an aerophone. Split strips of bamboo are glued into a tapering conical tube; it has no keys, seven fingerholes and an oval blowing edge, a narrow “throat” inside the bore, and a lead plug wrapped in paper and wax in the head joint. The player blows across the instrument and can produce a high, forceful note rich in high harmonics. It is used in the traditional theatre music of Nō, kabuki, yosebayashi and Gionbayashi, and was created by Kan'ami and Zeami in the fifteenth century.
